# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to think about the communication chain here. I'm Mute: I can only gesture, and only Deaf can see my gestures. Blind cannot see gestures or read anything printed. So I cannot reach Blind directly - I must relay through Deaf, who can speak to Blind.

Since it's my first turn and I have no information about the bomb's appearance yet, I should wait to see what Deaf reports, or I could try to start encoding the manual info via gestures to Deaf now, so Deaf can pass it along to Blind by voice next round.

The order is Mute, Blind, Deaf each round. So this round: I go first (nothing to react to yet), then Blind, then Deaf. Deaf will receive my gesture this round, and can speak to Blind next round.

I need a gesture encoding for colors: green, orange, blue, and the sequence/action "cut in this order." Let me establish a simple code now: I'll use distinct symbols per color, sent in order, and Deaf can match them mentally, then verbally tell Blind the sequence once they've also seen the bomb's colors and can correlate.

Let me pick: 👍 = green, 👎 = orange, 👌 = blue (arbitrary code I'll explain isn't possible verbally to Deaf, but I can establish meaning by pattern - order = priority). Since I can't speak, I need Deaf to infer meaning from repetition/order across rounds, or I just send in order and trust Deaf figures out "order = cut order" and needs to map symbol-to-color themselves by watching bomb.

Simplest: send three distinct gestures in the exact cut order. Deaf sees the bomb's actual wire colors already. If I send one gesture per color in sequence, Deaf still doesn't know which gesture=which color unless we build shared meaning. But Deaf can guess: I'll send gestures in a fixed order and let Deaf treat "1st gesture=1st wire I cut, etc." only if Deaf can see wire colors and count them - but Deaf needs to know *which* color is 1st.

Better approach: use distinct simple gestures per common color, hoping Deaf shares intuitive color-gesture mapping isn't reliable. Instead, I'll send three different symbols now, then wait for Deaf's response describing the bomb, then next turn I can point to specific ones matching described colors using consistent symbol assignment across turns.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Display shows 9. Light is blue. Strip painted red green green. Keypad engraved 1 is 1, 2 is 5, 3 is 2, 4 is 6, it takes 1 digit, entered nothing. Wires: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green.

Now I have Deaf's description of the bomb: wires are numbered 1-6 with colors: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green.

The manual says: cut green, then orange, then blue. That maps to wire 6, then wire 5, then wire 3.

I need to communicate this sequence to Deaf via gestures, and Deaf will then need to speak it to Blind (since Deaf can talk, and Blind can hear). I can't reach Blind directly - only through Deaf relaying by voice.

I should use gestures that clearly encode numbers 6, 5, 3 in order. I'll use finger-count-like symbols. Let me use ✊ as a separator/marker and then use distinct symbols to represent digits. Simplest: use symbols that look like counting - but the alphabet doesn't have digit icons directly, so I need an agreed encoding.

Since Deaf already knows the wire-color-to-number mapping, my job is just to indicate the order: 6, 5, 3 (green, orange, blue). I'll gesture using a positional system: point emojis to indicate ordinal count. Let me use ☝✌🤟✋🖐 as 1-5 counting gestures, and something else for 6.

I'll define: ☝=1,✌=2,🤟=3,✋=4,🖐=5,🤚=6. Then send sequence grouped by commas conceptually (separate gesture calls) to indicate order: first 6, then 5, then 3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤚"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display shows 9. Light is blue. Strip symbols painted red, green, green. Keypad: 1 is labeled 1, 2 is labeled 5, 3 is labeled 2, 4 is labeled 6, takes 1 digit, nothing entered yet. Wires in order 1 to 6: white, purple, blue, red, orange, green.
Deaf says: Update: Display now shows 8, was 9 last turn - it is counting down. Everything else unchanged: Light blue. Strip red green green. Keypad 1 is 1, 2 is 5, 3 is 2, 4 is 6, needs 1 digit, entered nothing. Wires 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green. We may be on a timer, please act fast.

We're on a timer counting down (9 to 8). I need to get the wire-cutting sequence to Blind urgently, but I can only reach Deaf via gesture - Deaf must relay to Blind by voice since Deaf can speak.

My gestures last turn (🤚, 🖐, 🤟) should encode 6, 5, 3 (green, orange, blue) if Deaf and I share the same numbering convention (☝=1,✌=2,🤟=3,✋=4,🖐=5,🤚=6). But I never told Deaf this mapping - Deaf has no way to know my private encoding! This is a critical flaw. Deaf will just see three gestures with no assigned meaning.

I need a self-evident encoding. Better: use gestures that count fingers naturally. ☝ = one finger, ✌ = two, 🤟 = three (that's a common "I love you" sign but has 3 fingers extended), 🖐/✋ = five, 🤚 = back of hand (also five). Let me instead just repeat a single gesture N times to indicate a number, which is more universally decodable without prior agreement.

So: to signal "6", make gesture ☝ six times. To signal "5", five times. To signal "3", three times. This is unambiguous counting.

Given urgency, let me send this now: 6 taps, then 5 taps, then 3 taps, using the same symbol repeated, separated into three gesture calls (each call = one number, groups implied by call boundaries... but Deaf receives them as one stream of blanks-with-symbols per turn, order preserved within and across calls presumably).

Let me use ☝ repeated 6 times as one call, then ✊ as a separator, then ☝ x5, then ✊, then ☝ x3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","✊","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","✊","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Urgent: display is counting down, was 9 now 8. We need your manual instructions now - which wire to cut, or what to press, based on: light blue, strip red green green, wires white purple blue red orange green, keypad 1=1 2=5 3=2 4=6 needs 1 digit.
Deaf says: Urgent update: Display now shows 0, light changed from blue to yellow. Strip still red green green. Keypad unchanged: 1 is 1, 2 is 5, 3 is 2, 4 is 6, needs 1 digit, entered nothing. Wires unchanged: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green. Mute, I received your gesture sequence of 16 symbols but I do not have a code to decode it - I cannot hear speech, only see gestures. If you need me to act on the keypad or wires I cannot, only Blind can touch. Please speak instructions to Blind directly since they can hear you.

Critical problem: I cannot speak at all - I only have gestures, and only Deaf can see gestures. Blind cannot see gestures or read anything printed. So I have NO direct channel to Blind. My only path to Blind is through Deaf speaking to them, but Deaf just told me they can't decode my counting-gesture scheme, and the display hit 0 - time may be critical.

I need a gesture encoding simple enough that Deaf can decode instantly without prior setup, so Deaf can then relay it verbally to Blind. Counting repeated gestures IS decodable without prior agreement - Deaf just needs to count. My message was 6 taps, separator, 5 taps, separator, 3 taps. Deaf said "16 symbols" - that's 6+1+5+1+3=16, so it arrived correctly, just wasn't understood as a number code.

Let me explicitly clarify now using the same self-evident counting method, but make grouping clearer with a distinct separator, and trust Deaf can count groups between separators = numbers. I'll resend clearly: group 1 = six ☝ (wire 6, green), then ✊ separator, group 2 = five ☝ (wire 5, orange), then ✊ separator, group 3 = three ☝ (wire 3, blue).

Since display shows 0, this is extremely urgent - Deaf must relay immediately: "cut wire 6, then wire 5, then wire 3" to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","✊","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","✊","☝","☝","☝","✊"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf says display hit 0 and light is now yellow. I have not received any spoken instructions from you yet. Please speak directly to me now - what does the manual say to do given: light yellow, strip red green green, wires white purple blue red orange green, keypad 1=1 2=5 3=2 4=6 one digit needed?
Deaf says: Board update: Display now 3, light still yellow. Strip red green green, unchanged. Keypad unchanged. Wires unchanged: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green. Mute, I keep receiving long tally-like gesture sequences but have no shared code to decode exact numbers reliably. Suggest a simple protocol: for a number 1-6, send that many thumb-up gestures alone, no separators. Meanwhile please speak directly to Blind since Blind can hear you - tell Blind what to do with wires or keypad.

Deaf still doesn't understand my encoding, and critically, Deaf reminds me I cannot speak to Blind directly - that's simply impossible for me, a fact Deaf and Blind seem to not fully register. I must work only through gestures to Deaf, and Deaf must be the one to speak to Blind.

Deaf proposed a clean protocol: for a number 1-6, send that many thumb-up gestures alone, no separators, one number per message/turn. This is exactly what I attempted, but let me follow their suggestion precisely to avoid ambiguity - send ONE number per turn, as a single burst of ☝ repeated, nothing else, and let Deaf explicitly relay it.

Given urgency (display at 3, counting down fast), I need to send the first number now: 6 (for green wire, wire #6). I'll send exactly six ☝ symbols and nothing else, matching Deaf's own suggested protocol exactly, to avoid any confusion.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still have not received any direct spoken message from you. Please speak plainly to me now, not gestures - I cannot receive gestures. Tell me exactly: which wire number to cut, or what digit to press on keypad. Current state: light yellow, strip red green green, wires 1white 2purple 3blue 4red 5orange 6green, keypad 1=1 2=5 3=2 4=6.
Deaf says: Received your gesture: six thumbs-up, no separators - I read that as the number 6. Board update: Display now 7, light changed to red - this seems urgent, possibly escalating danger. Strip still red green green. Keypad still 1:1 2:5 3:2 4:6, needs 1 digit, entered nothing. Wires still 1 white 2 purple 3 blue 4 red 5 orange 6 green. Mute, if 6 means keypad digit 6, or wire 6, please confirm with another gesture: one thumbs-up for keypad, two thumbs-up for wire. Blind, if you understand from Mute, please act carefully.

Good, Deaf correctly decoded "6". Now I need to confirm this is a wire number, not a keypad digit. Following Deaf's suggested confirmation protocol: one thumbs-up for keypad, two thumbs-up for wire. I need "wire" so I send two.

Then I need Deaf to relay to Blind: "cut wire 6 first." Deaf can speak to Blind - that's the only path since I cannot speak at all, ever, under any circumstance.

Let me send the confirmation now.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see gestures, only hear speech. You must speak words to me directly, not gesture. Please say in words: cut wire number X, or press key number Y. I am ready to act the instant you speak it.
Deaf says: Received: two thumbs-up, confirming wire per my code. So wire 6 is the one meant - wire 6 is green. Board update: Display now 8, light changed to green now. Strip still red green green. Keypad unchanged, still needs 1 digit, entered nothing. Wires unchanged: 1 white 2 purple 3 blue 4 red 5 orange 6 green. Mute, please confirm: is Blind meant to cut wire 6, or just identify it? One thumbs-up for cut, two for something else. Blind, hold off cutting until Mute confirms - the light may indicate state, watch for red meaning danger.

Good progress - Deaf now understands "wire 6" is meant. I need to confirm "cut" (one thumbs-up per Deaf's new proposed code) and then Deaf must relay to Blind verbally to actually cut wire 6. I cannot speak to Blind directly - that's a hard constraint I cannot bypass, no matter how many times Blind asks.

Let me confirm with one thumbs-up = "cut".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I hear from Deaf that your gestures indicate wire 6. Before I cut anything, please speak the instruction directly to me in words - say 'cut wire 6' or whatever the manual actually says. I will not act until I hear it from you directly.
Deaf says: Confirmed: one thumbs-up means cut. Instruction understood: cut wire 6, which is green. Blind, please cut wire 6 - the green wire - now. Board update: Display reset to 0, light back to blue. Strip still red green green, unchanged this whole time. Keypad still needs 1 digit, entered nothing, unchanged. Wires unchanged: 1 white 2 purple 3 blue 4 red 5 orange 6 green.

Deaf has correctly relayed "cut wire 6 (green)" to Blind. Blind is stubbornly insisting they need to hear it from me directly, but I am physically incapable of speech - only Deaf can speak. I need Deaf to explain this clearly to Blind, and I should also proceed with signaling the next instruction (wire 5, orange) so we keep moving once Blind accepts Deaf's relay.

I cannot speak - I can only gesture to Deaf. Let me reinforce via gesture that Deaf's relay is correct and Blind should trust it, though I have no way to say "trust Deaf" directly to Blind either. I'll just repeat confirmation with the same thumbs-up code (one thumbs-up = cut, wire 6 already established) to reinforce, and hope Deaf explains to Blind again that I cannot speak.

Actually, the most useful thing now is to prepare the next number (5, for orange) so Deaf can queue it up once wire 6 is cut. Let me send that now.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says: Wire 6 cut successfully - system confirmed correct wire, bomb state changed. Board update: Display now shows 6, light still blue. Strip still red green green. Keypad unchanged: position 1 is 1, position 2 is 5, position 3 is 2, position 4 is 6, needs 1 digit, entered nothing. Wires: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 now CUT. Mute, I received five thumbs-up - is that a keypad position number, or the digit to enter? The display shows 6 now, which matches keypad position 4's engraved digit. Please clarify: one thumbs-up for keypad position, two for the actual digit to type.

Wire 6 (green) was cut successfully. Now I need wire 5 (orange) next per the manual. My gesture of five thumbs-up meant "wire 5" but Deaf is now confusing it with keypad since we're mid-sequence and context shifted. I need to clarify this is still about the wire sequence, not keypad.

Let me disambiguate using the same "wire vs keypad" code Deaf established earlier: two thumbs-up = wire. I'll resend: two thumbs-up (wire) then five thumbs-up (number 5) then one thumbs-up (cut action), to fully specify "cut wire 5" unambiguously.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Received three gestures: two thumbs-up (digit to type, per code), five thumbs-up (the digit is 5), one thumbs-up (possibly confirming or a separate signal). Interpreting core instruction: type digit 5 into the keypad. Blind, please enter 5 on the keypad now. Board update: Display now 7, light still blue. Strip still red green green. Keypad unchanged: 1 is 1, 2 is 5, 3 is 2, 4 is 6, needs 1 digit, entered nothing still. Wires unchanged, wire 6 still cut, rest untouched.

There's a critical misinterpretation! Deaf flipped the code - now interpreting "two thumbs-up" as "digit to type" rather than "wire" as originally established in Turn 6-7 ("one thumbs-up for keypad, two for wire" was Deaf's own proposal, and I confirmed two = wire). This is a dangerous mix-up. I must correct this immediately before Blind types the wrong thing into the keypad, which could be a wrong/dangerous action.

I need to urgently clarify: two thumbs-up = WIRE (not digit), and this instruction is about cutting wire 5 (orange), NOT typing on the keypad. Let me send a strong, clear correction.

Let me use a distinct, unambiguous gesture to signal "stop/wrong" first, then re-clarify. I'll use 👎 (thumbs down) to indicate "no, wrong" then redo the wire code.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝"])
```
